title: Demand-cluster rightsizer and actionable alerts for dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: customers with Dedicated pools struggle to choose commitment sizes that balance cost and burst capacity. Existing advisors focus on aggregate utilization and single-number recommendations; they under-index on mixed workloads (steady background traffic + irregular bursty endpoints) and on latency-driven SLA purposes. Goal: build a demand-cluster based rightsizer that groups routes/patterns by demand shape and SLA sensitivity, simulates slab allocations per cluster, and produces per-pool recommended commits and automated alerts with clear runbook actions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clustering pipeline runs daily on historical 90d traces and produces <=10 clusters per pool with human-readable labels (e.g., steady-background, nightly-batch, interactive-burst).
- For each cluster compute recommended slab count for target SLOs (P95 latency and throughput SLO) and a suggested headroom fraction (e.g., 10-30%).
- Console table: show per-pool current commit, recommended commit, delta %, expected monthly cost delta, and confidence score.
- Alerts: trigger when observed utilization deviates from recommendation by >20% for 7 days or when burst percentile exceeds recommended headroom for 3 consecutive daily windows.
- Simulation harness: replay last 30 days against recommended commit and report expected SLA violations and cost delta.
- PR with experiments and a prototype Grafana dashboard merged and end-to-end test added to integration suite.
technical_notes:
Approach: 1) Feature extraction: aggregate time-series per route/pool at 1m resolution (rps, 95/99 latency, seq len distribution). 2) Demand clustering: use DBSCAN then silhouette-based pruning to form workload clusters; fallback to k-means when noisy. 3) Rightsize calc: for each cluster run a stochastic capacity simulation using current batching/kv cache behavior to estimate slabs required to meet chosen SLOs under given headroom percentiles. 4) Confidence: compute bootstrap CI from segmented traces; mark low-confidence when traces <14 days. 5) API/Console: expose /api/v1/rightsizer/{pool} returning recommended_commit, rationale, simulation_summary. 6) Alerts: integrate with existing fleet-mon engine to create automated tickets when drift sustained. Edge cases: newly created pools (cold start) must default to conservative commit until 7d of data. Quantization: account for alternative model variants (smaller quantized variant requires different slab estimate) via model-profile mapping. Performance: pipeline should process 90d traces for a 5k-pool account in under 2 hours using our batch infra.
Implementation phases: prototype (PoC clustering + local sim), pilot with 3 customers, GA rollout with auto-suggest and opt-in autoscale rule generation.
